instructions: Put the chicken thighs in a large pot with 7 cups of water. Add half the onion, the celery cut in large pieces, the 3 garlic cloves, 1 of the carrots in large pieces, the parsley sprigs, bay leaves, thyme, marjoram and peppercorns.

Bring it to a boil over high heat, then turn it down to low. Partly cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest thigh: it's done when the juices run clear.
Skim the foam and fat off the top with a spoon. Lift the chicken onto a plate. Strain the broth into a clean pot and throw out the vegetables, herbs and peppercorns.
While the chicken cools, cut the remaining 2 carrots and the zucchini into 1/2-inch rounds, chop the rest of the onion, and cut each ear of corn into 3 pieces.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, corn and 1 1/2 tsp salt to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the zucchini and cook for 10 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.

Meanwhile, cook the rice. Rinse 1 cup of rice, add it to a small pot with 2 cups of water and 1/2 tsp salt, and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Remove the skin and bones from the chicken and shred the meat into bite-size pieces. Add it to the soup and warm it for 2 minutes. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro and cut the limes into wedges. Put rice in each bowl, ladle the soup over it, and serve with the cilantro and lime wedges.

For a week of lunches, cool the soup and keep the rice in a separate container. The soup keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days, or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat a portion on the stove and add the rice to your bowl.
method_notes: Bossy Kitchen is the lead: a broth simmered from bone-in thighs with celery, onion, carrot, garlic and herbs, then strained, with fresh carrots, zucchini and corn simmered in it, and rice, lime and cilantro in the bowl. I scaled it from 6 to 4 and dropped the avocado and tortillas. Stacy Lyn Harris agrees on the method and serves it over rice with garnishes. Neither has 20+ ratings (5 stars from 1 each), and the busier caldo pages were blocked, so this is a fallback on the best-read versions. RecipeTin Eats has no caldo de pollo.
